scope: Bibliography entries 10–19: existence, primary metadata, publication status, abstract/content fit. No execution or replication of cited experiments.

notes: The arXiv abstract and paper bodies give opposite author order for entry 11; this is a source conflict, not evidence of an erroneous citation.
OpenReview forum/PDF endpoints returned browser challenges; entries 15 and 18 were instead checked against arXiv publication statements and, for 15, the author-hosted published PDF.
Title capitalization, accents, and inclusion of a middle initial are not counted as substantive errors.

references.title: Exploiting Lower Precision Arithmetic in Solving Symmetric Positive Definite Linear Systems and Least Squares Problems
evidence: Publisher gives matching title, two authors in this order, volume 43 issue 1, pages A258–A277; published online 19 January 2021.
Abstract describes low-precision Cholesky factors as preconditioners in GMRES iterative refinement, diagonal shifts/scaling, and extension to well-conditioned least squares through normal equations.
references.manuscript_use: Related-work paragraph lines 454–456 cites conditioning, roundoff and precision allocation.
references.boundary: Does not establish this manuscript’s neural-model gradient/update discrepancies or FP32/FP64 stage-factorial results.

references.title: Differentiating Through Linear Solvers
evidence: Both arXiv abstract records list Paul Hovland then Jan Hückelheim; both PDFs and HTML bodies list Jan then Paul with equal contribution. The manuscript follows the abstract record, so its order cannot fairly be called a confirmed error.
The v1 PDF contains an ICML 2023 / PMLR 202 template footer, removed in v2. It is not evidence of publication in those proceedings; the cited arXiv 2024 status is appropriate.
Studies low-level differentiation through GMRES, TFQMR and BiCGStab versus equation-level differentiation on 65 SuiteSparse matrices; primarily forward mode.
references.manuscript_use: Line 95 supports the warning that forward agreement does not establish derivative agreement; lines 464–465 explicitly describe implementation-versus-equation differentiation, primarily forward mode.
references.support_assessment: Accurate description in related work; valid conceptual precedent for separating solution and derivative accuracy.
references.boundary: Not an experiment on FP32 versus FP64 Cholesky stages, restored Adam/AdamW updates, or long-horizon learned-ridge training. Treating it as direct evidence for those details would overextend it.
issues: Source-internal author order discrepancy. Recommend a version-specific link or note if exact author order needs resolution; do not penalize the manuscript solely for following arXiv metadata.

references.title: A taxonomy of automatic differentiation pitfalls
references.venue: WIREs Data Mining and Knowledge Discovery
evidence: Publisher lists these six authors in this order, first publication 2 September 2024, issue November/December 2024, 14(6):e1555.
Categorizes pitfalls involving functions, abstraction and operator precision, including linear solvers, discretization, fixed-point loops and floating-point effects.
references.manuscript_use: Lines 462–464 cite numerical AD pitfalls, including incompletely converged iterative solvers.
references.boundary: A taxonomy with examples is not a universal theorem that AD gradients are unreliable, and it does not measure this manuscript’s actual optimizer updates.

references.title: Matrix Backpropagation for Deep Networks With Structured Layers
references.venue: Proceedings of the IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision (ICCV)
evidence: CVF official paper page explicitly matches title, ordered authors, conference year and pages 2965–2973.
Develops matrix backpropagation for global structured operations, with second-order pooling and normalized-cut segmentation experiments.
arXiv 1509.07838 is an extended version with a different title; that title difference does not make the cited ICCV record wrong.
references.manuscript_use: Lines 445–447 group it with structured linear-algebra layers embedded in end-to-end learning.
references.support_assessment: Appropriate historical background for differentiable matrix computations.
references.boundary: Does not by itself support specific Gram-solver precision-placement or optimizer-equivalence claims.

references.title: A Study of BFLOAT16 for Deep Learning Training
evidence: arXiv v1 29 May 2019, latest v3 13 June 2019; title, all 19 authors and order match, apart from manuscript inclusion of D. as the first author’s middle initial. This name variant is not a substantive discrepancy.
Studies BFLOAT16 tensors with FP32 accumulation/selected state across vision, language, GAN and recommendation workloads; broad comparable task results do not assert identical numerical trajectories.
references.manuscript_use: Lines 457–458 group higher-precision accumulation, master weights, loss scaling and tensor assignment precedents.
references.support_assessment: Supports mixed-precision tensor flow and accumulation background. The grouped sentence should not be read as saying each cited work advocates every listed technique.
references.boundary: The BFLOAT16 paper emphasizes avoiding additional hyperparameter changes in its experiments; loss scaling in the grouped sentence is most directly associated with FP16 work such as Micikevicius. No citation mismatch established.

references.title: Training with Mixed-Precision Floating-Point Assignments
references.access_notes: OpenReview forum/PDF access returned browser challenge. arXiv says Published in TMLR; author-hosted final PDF says Published in Transactions on Machine Learning Research (06/2023) and gives the identical OpenReview ID.
evidence: Ordered three authors and title match.
Studies tensor-level precision assignments and memory/accuracy tradeoffs for CNN training on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 and ImageNet.
references.boundary: Not a direct prior test of Gram-stage Cholesky precision and matched restored adaptive-optimizer updates.

references.title: Deep learning for universal linear embeddings of nonlinear dynamics
references.access_notes: Direct Nature URL encountered an identity-provider redirect; publisher content retrieved through DOI search result and matched to primary arXiv record.
evidence: Publisher record gives matching title, ordered authors, 9:4950, published 23 November 2018.
Uses modified autoencoders and an auxiliary network to learn Koopman eigenfunction representations including systems with continuous spectra.
references.manuscript_use: Lines 450–452 cite finite-dimensional Koopman approximations and learned dynamical representations.
references.boundary: This citation is not evidence for numerical precision-induced training inequivalence; the manuscript uses it as representation background.

references.title: Pointer Sentinel Mixture Models
evidence: arXiv v1 submitted 26 September 2016, with matching title and four authors in this order.
Introduces pointer-sentinel language modeling and the WikiText corpus.
references.manuscript_use: Line 1017 attributes WikiText-2; manuscript explicitly says its 1,000 held-out records come from the filtered training split, not official validation.
references.boundary: Citing the 2016 preprint is valid; it does not validate the manuscript’s custom split or imply benchmark-comparable official validation scores.

references.title: Mixed Precision Training
references.access_notes: OpenReview forum/PDF returned browser challenge. arXiv comments explicitly say Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2018; v3 dated 15 February 2018.
evidence: Title and all 11 ordered authors match.
Uses half-precision training tensors, a single-precision master copy of weights and loss scaling; validates multiple network families.
references.manuscript_use: Lines 457–458 cite mixed-precision accumulation/master weights/loss scaling.
references.support_assessment: Directly supports the master-weight and loss-scaling background.
references.boundary: Matching task accuracy under mixed precision does not assert exact gradients, updates or trajectories; do not read it as conflicting with the present paper merely because it reports comparable final accuracy.

references.title: Differentiation of the Cholesky decomposition
evidence: arXiv v1 submitted 24 February 2016; matching title and sole author.
Derives symbolic and algorithmic Cholesky differentiation rules, with blocked algorithms based on LAPACK DPOTRF and BLAS matrix operations.
references.manuscript_use: Line 464 says Murray derives Cholesky differentiation rules.
references.boundary: Derivative formula correctness does not certify numerical stability for every input or neural-training equivalence across precision routes.
